transcript:
User: We have a girl at the front desk, she picks up fine. Not sure why I'd need this.
Agent: Got it, if she’s handling calls well, that’s good news.  

Mhm—when she steps away (lunch, bathroom, running an errand, out sick), what happens to calls that come in during those gaps?
User: We just call people back when she's unavailable. It’s worked fine for us so far.
Agent: Makes sense, a lot of places try to catch up later by calling folks back.  

So when you return those calls, how often do you find the person’s already gone with someone else or just doesn’t pick up anymore?
User: We never really counted how many calls we miss or lose. Seems like a solution looking for a problem.
Agent: Got it, I hear you—it can feel that way if you haven’t seen a clear gap yet.  

So if we kept this really simple: on a busy day, what’s your best guess on how many calls go to voicemail or get a call-back instead of being answered live?
User: Maybe about 15 missed calls a week, but we usually handle them with call-backs.
Agent: Got it—so roughly 15 a week that don’t get answered live and you try to catch them later.  

Out of those 15, if you had to guess, how many turn into actual bookings or paying customers versus people you never connect with again?
User: I'd say maybe half of them would book, but we manage alright with follow-ups.
Agent: Got it—so maybe 7–8 of those missed callers each week turn into actual bookings, and the rest just…fade out.  

If you could turn a few more of those into confirmed appointments without adding work to your front desk, would that be worth exploring, or does it genuinely feel like a non-issue for you right now?
User: Alright, as a backup layer I can see it. Book your demo. Call me at +16175550005.
Agent: Got it, that makes sense — using this as a backup layer is exactly where Dialux shines, catching those calls your front desk can’t get to in time.

Jay will give you a live demo and walk through how we turn those missed calls into bookings and revenue, then you can decide if it’s a fit.

We’ll call you at +1 617-555-0005 for that demo — thanks for taking the time today, and talk soon.
